chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from whom he mentioned from Aban from Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whatever food, goods, or things differ in quality so that one is superior to the other, there is no harm in selling it, two of the same kind for one, hand to hand; but as for deferment (delay in delivery), it is not valid.

key_terms.مِثْلَيْنِ بِمِثْلٍ: two of the same kind for one (referring to quantity exchange)
key_terms.يَتَفَاضَلُ: to differ in quality or superiority

ai.seo_question: Can I sell two high-quality dates for one low-quality date if I pay immediately?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of 'like for like' in *Bay' al-Fadl* applies strictly to uniform commodities, allowing variable qualities to be exchanged in unequal ratios (e.g., two inferior for one superior) as long as the transaction is immediate (*yadan bi-yad*). This ruling distinguishes between the uncertainty of quality differences and the riba associated with deferred delivery of homogeneous goods, a key principle in Shia fiqh regarding commodity trading.
